takeaways: Power Automate flows are non-human workers with identities and permissions, so they must be governed like infrastructure rather than cleaned up after incidents.

A governable estate rests on four planes: where flows live (environments), what they touch (DLP and connectors), who owns them (identities and an ownership register) and how they are watched (inventory, telemetry, cost).
Start with an inventory and ownership check, then add environments and a DLP baseline, solutions and pipelines, and finally monitoring, license gates and joiner-mover-leaver automation.
hook: Somewhere in your tenant a flow is running under the account of someone who left months ago. This episode is for Power Platform admins, platform teams and IT leaders who need to govern Power Automate at enterprise scale. You get a practical model covering environments, DLP, connection ownership, solutions and pipelines, monitoring, licensing and orphaned flows, plus where to start on Monday.
